title: The importance of being external. Methodological insights for the external validation of machine learning models in medicine
journal_or_venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine

content.abstract_summary: A methodological paper on external validation of medical ML models that examines how training-validation similarity affects generalizability and proposes assessing discrimination, utility, and calibration together.
key_findings: External validation should assess more than discrimination alone.
Dataset similarity and covariate shift affect apparent generalizability.
Discrimination, utility, and calibration provide complementary validation dimensions.
limitations: General medical ML framework rather than pharmacometric or hybrid-model-specific guidance.

gaps_addressed: External validation, calibration, and decision-relevant evaluation for hybrid PK/PD models

provenance.notes: Focused validation/transportability search; used to define evaluation-card dimensions.
